newsitem.title: USA: Los Alamos lab workers fired in Internet sting.
newsitem.headline: Los Alamos lab workers fired in Internet sting.

text.p: Four employees of the Los Alamos National Laboratory in New Mexico were fired and 10 others disciplined for allegedly surfing the Internet for pornography, online shopping and other personal sites, a lab spokesman said on Friday.

Computer-security specialists monitoring lab network traffic netted the workers during an ongoing investigation of unauthorised use of lab computers to access the Internet, John Gustafson, a lab spokesman, said.
"The majority were visiting adult-oriented sites," Gustafson said. "We're talking about multiple repeated visits ... It could have been hundreds of times."
The workers were using some of the lab's 25,000 computers to browse the Internet, a vast global computer network run by universities, governments and private organisations.

A similar crackdown at Sandia National Laboratories in Albuquerque, New Mexico, had found visits to pornographic sites by as many as 100 workers, and a computer technician at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in California was prosecuted for saving and distributing more than 90,000 pornographic images on a lab computer, lab officials said.
